name: Hummus
steps: Use fully cooked chickpeas that crush easily between your fingers; drain and rinse them. Keep a few aside for garnish. This recipe starts with cooked chickpeas, not dry beans.
Blend tahini and lemon juice until creamy, scraping down the sides once. The mixture may thicken at first; continue until evenly combined.
Add chickpeas, cumin powder, salt and about half the measured water. Blend until smooth, stopping to scrape the sides rather than leaving unblended pieces near the top.
Add the remaining water a little at a time until the hummus forms soft swirls when stirred. Blend in the olive oil and taste before adjusting seasoning.
Spoon into a serving bowl and make a shallow swirl with the back of a spoon. Finish with the reserved chickpeas; keep covered and refrigerated if preparing ahead.
tips: Use fully cooked chickpeas. Plain tahini contains sesame.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
